title: Exploring the Dose–Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Series of Meta-Regressions
population: Training studies of failure versus non-failure, velocity loss and set structures, pooled in exploratory meta-regressions; participant details are not summarized in the abstract.
key_findings: Repetitions in reserve were estimated for each training condition from the study descriptions and modelled as a continuous dose.
Strength gains showed a negligible relationship with estimated repetitions in reserve: similar across a wide range.
Hypertrophy increased as sets ended closer to failure in every best-fit model; the authors stress that the exact relationship remains unclear and the analysis is exploratory.
methods: Series of multilevel meta-regressions of estimated repetitions in reserve against strength and hypertrophy, adjusted for load, method of volume equating, duration and training status, with sensitivity analyses.
limitations: Repetitions in reserve were estimated by the authors, not measured; overall model fit was modest; exploratory by the authors' own description.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
